generations.memory_31: SMB signup simplification worked: signups rose 15%, activation 9%, and qualified revenue 4%. Retention dipped 1%, so treat this as an SMB-specific win rather than a cross-segment finding.
generations.memory_44: The enterprise sales-assisted CTA reduced signups by 12% but increased qualified leads 24% and qualified revenue 18%, with no retention change. Confirmed for enterprise; it is not a broad signup-growth tactic.
generations.memory_57: Referral incentives were effective in established accounts, lifting referral starts 21%, qualified revenue 7%, and retention 2%. The impact was concentrated in accounts more than six months old.
generations.memory_73: A 40% discount drove strong initial acquisition—signups up 31% and qualified revenue up 18%—but 30-day retention fell 12%. The cohort failed to make it through the first renewal cycle, so do not use targeted discounting as a sustainable-growth strategy.
generations.memory_86: Shortening onboarding improved completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and lifted 30-day retention 3%. This result is confirmed and supports continuing the shorter flow.
generations.memory_91: In-product activation messaging increased week-one engagement 11%, activation 6%, and 30-day retention 1%. The experiment is confirmed, with modest but positive downstream retention impact.
